foodDescription: A thin, crisp pancake of chickpea flour, water, and olive oil, baked on a huge copper pan in a wood oven. Cut into pieces, peppered, and eaten hot with your fingers.
Bread dough topped with onions cooked slowly until sweet, black olives, and anchovies. Sold by the slice at bakeries and markets.
Tomatoes, raw vegetables, hard-boiled eggs, black olives, and anchovies or tuna, dressed with olive oil. In Nice, cooked potatoes and green beans are considered a mistake.
A round roll soaked in olive oil and filled with the ingredients of a salade niçoise. Nice’s picnic sandwich, best after it has sat for an hour.
Small tomatoes, zucchini, onions, and peppers stuffed with meat, herbs, and breadcrumbs, then baked. A classic family dish, eaten warm or cold.
Eggplant, zucchini, peppers, tomatoes, and onions stewed in olive oil. It comes from Nice, where cooks insist each vegetable be fried separately first.
Beef braised for hours in red wine with herbs and orange peel. The leftover sauce is used to fill ravioli, a reminder of Nice’s Italian past.
Zucchini blossoms dipped in batter and fried, sold in spring and summer at the markets and served as a starter.
A summer soup of beans, vegetables, and pasta, finished with pistou, a paste of basil, garlic, and olive oil, like pesto without nuts.
A surprising local dessert: Swiss chard mixed with raisins, pine nuts, apples, and sugar in a pastry crust, dusted with sugar.
An anise-flavored spirit mixed with cold water until it turns cloudy. The aperitif of southern France, drunk slowly on a terrace.
Wine from a tiny area of vineyards in the hills inside the city limits, one of the smallest wine appellations in France. Rare and mostly drunk locally.
